text:
为什么分数接近，不代表能力接近？

拿 GLM-5.2 和 Opus 4.8 比：SWE-Bench Pro 上 62.1 vs 69.2，就差 7 分，看着快追平了。但 GLM 激活 40B，Opus 闭源没公开、按万亿总参反推激活在数百 B——差一个数量级。

关键在激活参数。MoE 的总参扩的是知识存储，但每个 token 的有效推理算力由激活规模决定。窄域 agentic coding 可以用大规模 RL 把分数对齐到评测分布，刷到接近；但 per-token 容量是刷不上去的。

难度一拉就现形：编码综合 Fable 85.6、GLM 62.1，差 23 分；最难的 FrontierCode Diamond 连 Opus 都才 13.4，开源这梯队根本够不着。题越难、链路越长，40B 激活的天花板越藏不住。

所以账面 7 分是后训练对齐出来的，真实能力差距远不止于此。

text:
谷歌正在重组成立仅数月的 AI 编程突击队，以追赶 Anthropic。重组将扩大突击队工作范围，并由短期项目组调整为正式架构。

重组期间，谷歌遭遇两位核心研究员流失。上周，Transformer 奠基人之一 Noam Shazeer 突然离职加入 OpenAI，起因是谷歌合并计算资源限制了 Shazeer 的访问权限。周六，诺奖得主、DeepMind 副总裁 John Jumper 宣布加盟 Anthropic，离职前 Jumper 已被调至编程突击队。核心研究员离职导致 Alphabet 股价周一暴跌 5%。

改组核心是调整模型训练流程。谷歌将编程突击队拓展为中训练团队，介于预训练与后训练之间。中训练团队将接管过去由后训练团队负责的编程等模型能力扩展，后训练团队则专注于优化人机交互。通过细分阶段与理清分工，谷歌试图加速提升模型能力。

改组背后是编程已成为 AI 服务中最具价值的板块。Anthropic 凭借编程工具优势，上月年化收入已达 470 亿美元，是 2 月水平的三倍以上。相比之下，谷歌早期对编程投入不足，误认为强大的基础模型会自动掌握编程能力。尽管联合创始人 Sergey Brin 和 DeepMind 首席技术官 Koray Kavukcuoglu 曾亲自参与编程突击队，但谷歌编程应用进展不顺。Antigravity 工具发布初期因漏洞多反响平平，Gemini 3.5 Flash 也因定价偏高和回答迎合用户被开发者批评，而旗舰模型 Gemini 3.5 Pro 至今仍未推出。
https://t.co/LTn6PFeUYD

项志宇教授是 DeepSeek 创始人梁文锋在浙江大学期间的导师。

在浙大读研期间，梁文锋师从项志宇教授，专注于计算机视觉方向的研究，并于 2010 年于浙大硕士毕业。

从这位教授的简历来看，他的背景和研究方向含金量极高，确实非常契合培养顶级 AI 人才的土壤。

2002-2004 年期间，他先后在葡萄牙阿威罗大学机器人实验室以及美国俄亥俄州立大学电子与计算机工程系从事博士后研究。

项教授主持过多项国家自然科学基金联合重点项目、面上项目，并在 CVPR、ICRA、IROS 等计算机视觉与机器人领域的顶级国际会议和期刊上发表了数十篇高水平论文。

因为 DeepSeek 的爆火，作为创始人导师的学术主页也吸引了许多同学前去打卡，成为了学术界产业界硬核技术传承的一个缩影。

text:
任何横空出世的奇迹，追根溯源，都有迹可循。

仔细审视梁文锋当年的硕士论文题目，会发现一个极具前瞻性与宿命感的词眼：

低成本。

当我们在谈论 DeepSeek 如何打破垄断、重新定义大模型格局时，不要忘了，这背后的总指挥，曾经也是一个为了一篇浙大学报录用通知而欣喜若狂、为了导师“逐行指导代码”而心怀感恩的普通研究生。

在2010年，如何利用有限的硬件算力与低成本的摄像机实现精准的目标跟踪，是计算机视觉领域的经典工程难题。

而十六年后的今天，DeepSeek 之所以能够在中美 AI 大模型百团大战中异军突起，靠的恰恰是把算力经济学和极致能效比发挥到了人类顶尖水平。

在硅谷，我们崇尚用成千上万块最顶级的 GPU、消耗着堪比小城市的电量进行大模型暴力蒸馏时，DeepSeek 却硬是凭借着精妙的算法架构创新，用极其有限的算力成本，逼近甚至超越了耗资数十亿美元的闭源怪兽。

深入骨髓的对资源的极致榨取和对效率的绝对追求，早在 2010 年那台低成本摄像机的算法优化中，就已经埋下了技术基因种子。

从 2002 年考入浙大本科，到 2010 年硕士毕业，再到如今 DeepSeek 名震寰宇，梁文锋个人的二十几年，恰好完整契合了中国硬科技井喷式爆发的黄金周期。

quotedTweet.text:
项志宇教授是 DeepSeek 创始人梁文锋在浙江大学期间的导师。

在浙大读研期间，梁文锋师从项志宇教授，专注于计算机视觉方向的研究，并于 2010 年于浙大硕士毕业。

从这位教授的简历来看，他的背景和研究方向含金量极高，确实非常契合培养顶级 AI 人才的土壤。

2002-2004 年期间，他先后在葡萄牙阿威罗大学机器人实验室以及美国俄亥俄州立大学电子与计算机工程系从事博士后研究。

项教授主持过多项国家自然科学基金联合重点项目、面上项目，并在 CVPR、ICRA、IROS 等计算机视觉与机器人领域的顶级国际会议和期刊上发表了数十篇高水平论文。

因为 DeepSeek 的爆火，作为创始人导师的学术主页也吸引了许多同学前去打卡，成为了学术界产业界硬核技术传承的一个缩影。

text:
最近一个现象越来越普遍。

很多公司在招人时，把目标锁定在“落难凤凰”身上——大厂出来的、上一家公司刚裁员的高P、曾经带过几十人团队的负责人。

期望很直接：来了就要出业绩，三个月见效果，半年扭转局面。

逻辑听起来成立：能力强、经验足、现在要价还不高，性价比拉满。

但有个问题被忽略了。

凤凰落难，往往不是能力的问题。而是上一家公司业务调整、战略收缩、周期波动。大环境的事，个人扛不住。

可新东家给的条件是：环境变了，但你要拿出和鼎盛时期一样的结果。

text:
我之前就说过，对于竞赛选手，尤其是CMO金牌选手，再难的高考数学都是降维打击。
如果你参加过CMO但现在的高考数学没有148左右，那只能证明你太弱，并且你一定不是金牌或集训队选手。

在全国一卷 720 多万考生中斩获唯一的数学满分，这不仅需要绝对的实力，更需要极其恐怖的心理素质。

徐可能拿到 CMO金牌全国 167 名、浙江省队第 36 名，说明他的数学思维早已远远超越了高考的选拔标准。高考数学的压轴题对于竞赛金牌选手来说，在思维深度上通常是完全涵盖甚至是向下兼容的。

别忘了，在CMO还有至少166个人比他强，还有一众和他同层次的强者，而且很多都已经保送离开凡人之境去往清华姚班北大数院。能满分的不止他一个，只是他选择了留在战场，告诉人们：

这张2026全国1卷数学，是可以满分的。

quotedTweet.text:
来看看2026年最新出炉的浙江高考。

状元来自镇海蛟川的周凌宇，总分723分。
语文134分，数学148分，外语144分，物理100分，化学98分，生物99分。

这次的浙江高考，全省只有一个150分满分，来自温州知临，且此人为全国数学奥林匹克竞赛金牌，不过貌似总分没有上700分。我之前得到的小道消息没有错。

根据目前已知的全省高分段排位，可以看到分咬得非常之紧，尤其在700-720分之间。但状元貌似比较断档，715-723分之间唯有周凌宇一人，看来是实力超群。

可以看到，浙江数学的难度的确是极大，还记得6年前全省满分至少不会出现个位数甚至是只有一人的情况，高考数学改革后，必须拉开区分度，筛选理工素养，题目越来越反套路化，高分越来越稀有。

还记得自己几年前模拟考试做浙江高考数学的时候，也是咬紧牙关。但现在的题，比当年又灵活硬核了几倍有余。

text:
非常建议每一个选择计算机系的大学生，在大学时期将cs336啃完，不开中文字幕，只开英文字幕。啃完之后，你对LLM的理解和英语能力至少在国内前百分之1%。

这门课超过国内任何一所大学里面计算机的课程。

《Stanford CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch》 是一门斯坦福大学计算机科学系的课程，这门课每一年春季都会有，每一年都会在油管免费开放。

里面的内容非常前沿而且实用，目前油管上的版本是25年的版本，第一节课提到的模型已经是GPT-4。而与此同时，国内的计算机课程还在用着至少5年前的PPT。

依稀记得，我的第一节C语言课程，PPT的里面的演示系统是XP...

啃完CS336，你会收获LLM的全栈技术栈，从数据收集，清洗，模型训练，优化，评估到部署，Transforemer架构，注意力机制，各种目前最新的机器学习训练方法

这门课的目标就是从头让你手搓一个LLM，亲手实现完整的pipeline。

两位主要讲师：
1、Percy Liang
MIT 本科 + MEng，UC Berkeley 博士（2011）。曾在 Google 做 post-doc，后加入 Stanford 任教。

2、Tatsu
Harvard 本科（统计与数学），MIT 博士（co-advised by Tommi Jaakkola 和 David Gifford），之后在 Stanford 做 Percy Liang 和 John Duchi 的 post-doc

耐心啃完这个，所有计算机课程几乎都不需要上了...因为在过程中必然会遇到很多不懂的点，边学边查，然后顺带就把学校关于机器学习和深度学习的专业课给学完了。

如果刚上大一，可以先看cs50，然后再到cs336，先稍微打点计算机的基础。

与此同时，一定要把线性代数学好，将高数丢了都要把线性代数学好，线性代数是机器学习的底层DNA。

如果线性代数没有学好，会比较难理解神经网络，相当于没学好加减乘除就想去求导。

This is a new paradigm for interacting with Claude that is significantly more "inline" with all the other human activity org-wide. Once you do all of the under the hood engineering work to make this "just work" (e.g. across tools, integrations, compute environments, memory, security, etc.), Claude basically joins the team in a seamless way - you can talk to it as you would talk to a person and it can help with a very large variety of workloads.

Imo this is the 3rd major redesign of LLM UIUX. The first paradigm was that the LLM is a website you go to, the second was that it is an app you download to your computer. This third one is that it is a self-contained, persistent, asynchronous entity with org-wide tools and context, working alongside teams of humans. It really takes a while to wrap your head around it, but it works and it is awesome.

text:
不会还有人不知道吧——现在大学只有两个专业值得读。

一个是计算机。对智力要求比较高，但只要你7岁小学一年级开始编程，一直到22岁本科计算机毕业，16年的编程生涯，你相信我，只要你他妈坚持下来，傻子能成编程高手了。

只要你编程高手，在美国进大厂月薪1万美金税后，问题不大。如果你编程特别牛逼，擅长AI和AI Agent，那你放心，你前途无量，你一定是全人类最后被AI替代的人。

另一个是医学。医学不需要那么高的智力，但是要好的记忆力，服从性，医学就适合按住就班的学生，美国四年本科五年医学院，慢慢苦熬。只要熬下来，收入相当可观，你放心读医学，门槛吊打律师，老师，后者是最快被AI替代的职业，但医学因为跟人类健康挂钩，高度敏感，很难被替代。你想想大人物，总统总理是放心AI看病，还是50年经验的老医生看病？一目了然的事情。

其他所有专业，所有专业，全部是垃圾专业，没有任何区别。

你读其他任何专业，你还不如拿这些钱直接买美股，买纳斯达克，买OpenAi股票，买BTC，绝对收益率吊打你读本科然后老老实实工作四十年退休。

听懂了没？上大学，聪明人学计算机，普通人学医学，其他所有专业，有一个算一个，全是垃圾专业，骗钱专业，千万不要读！！！！！！

秘密其实是「盲水印」。

今天看到一个挺有意思的开源项目：blind_watermark（14k Stars）。

它和普通水印有什么不一样？

• 肉眼完全看不见（藏在频域里）
• 抗攻击能力很强：裁剪、加噪、压缩、甚至手机翻拍后依然能提取
• 纯 Python 实现，开箱即用

对做安全和内容保护的人来说，这个思路确实值得关注。

The future of software development is agentic, persistent, and cloud-native.

The future of software development is agentic, persistent, and cloud-native.

text:
There is a medical condition that makes human beings physically allergic to water. A single drop on their skin triggers agonizing, burning hives within minutes. Even their own sweat or tears can cause a severe reaction.

Imagine a life where taking a shower, walking in the rain, or crying causes your skin to erupt in intense, burning welts. This is the reality for people diagnosed with Aquagenic Urticaria. It is a profoundly rare condition, with fewer than 100 cases ever documented in medical history.

The condition is so precise that temperature does not matter. Whether the water is boiling hot, ice cold, distilled, or chemically pure, the biological reaction remains identical. Within 20 to 30 minutes of skin contact, tiny, highly irritating red hives called wheals break out across the body.

Because the human body is roughly 60 percent water, the internal mechanics of this condition seem impossible. Remarkably, patients can drink water without their stomach reacting, as the condition primarily targets the outer layers of the skin. However, swallowing can still feel incredibly uncomfortable if water touches their lips.

To survive daily life, individuals with Aquagenic Urticaria must develop extraordinary coping mechanisms. Showers are limited to just a few minutes, once or twice a week, requiring maximum speed. Physical exercise is heavily restricted because their own sweat will instantly trigger a painful reaction on their arms and torso.

Medical scientists are still uncovering exactly why this happens. The leading theory suggests that when water mixes with a specific substance on the skin's surface, it creates a microscopic toxin. The immune system detects this toxin, rushes into overdrive, and releases massive amounts of histamine, causing the skin to swell.

To counteract the daily threat, individuals rely on high-dose antihistamines and special skin barriers like petroleum jelly to deflect water droplets. Despite the immense daily challenges, those living with the condition show incredible human resilience, adapting seamlessly to a world covered in a substance they must actively avoid.

Through careful management, specialized medical routines, and sheer willpower, individuals with this condition live full, active lives while navigating a literal allergy to the modern world.

THE BORROWED VOICE
( is currently in editing ) 

Who speaks for the American truck driver when the driver behind the wheel is too busy working to be heard?

The Borrowed Voice examines how a Canadian-born former truck driver became one of the most recognized voices discussing the challenges facing American truckers, while many working drivers remained largely absent from the national conversation.

This is not a book about one man. It is a book about a system. It explores why certain voices rise, why others are ignored, and what happens when institutions, media outlets, industry organizations, and drivers themselves leave the microphone unattended.

Drawing from public records, interviews, industry events, media appearances, and the perspective of a driver with more than three decades behind the wheel, Will Cook asks difficult questions about representation, advocacy, accountability, and the future of independent trucking.

Whether readers agree with the conclusions or not, The Borrowed Voice challenges the industry to consider a simple question:

If the working driver is not leading the conversation about trucking, who is?

By Will Cook
A Driver’s Perspective
Expected Release: August 2026
Rollin Insight Media

Whether readers agree with the conclusions or not, The Borrowed Voice challenges the industry to consider a simple question:

If the working driver is not leading the conversation about trucking, who is?

By Will Cook
A Driver’s Perspective
Expected Release: August 2026
Rollin Insight Media

Why $LTH (Life Time Holdings) is a resilient buy in uncertain times—premium "athletic resorts" blending gym, spa, coworking & family vibes. Trading ~$29.80 (as of Feb '26), forward P/E ~17.5x, P/S ~2x—cheap vs. peers like $PLNT (26-31x). Consensus target ~$40 (35% upside), my high-conviction: $45+ on expansion beats & margin ramps.

Key thesis: $LTH operates as a premium "third space"—luxury athletic resorts that serve as essential community hubs for affluent members, blending top-tier fitness, spa, coworking, recovery, family activities, and social connection. This positions it far beyond a traditional gym: it's a lifestyle destination where people invest in physical/mental health, routine, purpose, and belonging.

In recessions, gyms (especially premium ones) don't just survive—they thrive. People cut discretionary luxuries like travel, dining out, and vacations first, but double down on affordable self-care, stress relief, mental health support, and daily structure. Historical proof: post-2008 financial crisis and during/post-COVID, $LTH saw churn stay remarkably low (<10%), with premium models gaining share as budget gyms faltered and consumers shifted toward higher-value experiences that deliver lasting wellness ROI. Recessions amplify the "health as priority" mindset, driving membership resilience and even acceleration in utilization.

This defensive moat combines with powerful secular tailwinds:
- AI-driven layoffs and potential UBI scenarios free up significant time → more availability for structured gym routines, social interaction, and personal development, boosting attendance, class participation, and ancillary spend.
- Permanent/hybrid WFH (still ~25-30% of workdays) continues to drive +15-20% daytime traffic surges → higher utilization of on-site cafes, coworking areas, spas, and mid-day classes, lifting non-dues revenue significantly.
- Broader cultural shift toward wellness: Gen Z and Millennials treat health/fitness as non-negotiable essentials (like food or housing), sustaining spend and enabling consistent mid-single-digit dues increases with minimal churn resistance.

Conclusion: a rare defensive growth story—recession-resilient demand profile + multiple accelerating growth levers (time abundance from tech disruption, WFH normalization, wellness megatrend) → strong same-store sales, membership momentum, and margin expansion through scale.

Trading at an attractive $29.80–$30 (Feb 2026 levels), forward P/E ~17x, P/S ~2x—meaningfully discounted vs. peers like $PLNT (26-31x). Consensus targets cluster ~$37–$41 (25-38% upside), with high-conviction bull case pushing $45+ on sustained beats from aggressive expansion (10 clubs in 2025 → 12-14 in 2026), efficiency gains (EBITDA margins ramping mid-20s → 27-28%), and earnings inflection as capex normalizes

Undervalued entry amid macro noise; positioned to outperform in soft-landing or mild downturn scenarios as consumers pivot to resilient, high-ROI self-investment. We are long $LTH

我做了一个 AI 中转站，今天正式开放：

https://t.co/8UjipCaDbh

一开始做这个站，想法很简单。

主要是我自己平时 Token 消耗量大，身边也有不少朋友一直用不上稳定的 Claude / GPT。不是订阅麻烦，就是各种限制；去找别的中转站，又总担心不靠谱、信息不安全。

所以干脆自己搭了一个。

很多人问：为什么敢用老叶的？

这个问题我也理解。毕竟 AI 中转站这东西，大家最怕的不是贵一点，而是不知道对面是谁。

我在币圈这么多年，别的不敢吹，信用两字一直是招牌。前两年比特币生态火的时候，做过 Ybot 铸造工具。起初也有人担心资产安全。

Ybot 到现在跑了两年多，上万人用过，很多人甚至直接在网站里填过钱包私钥，总资产少说也有几千万。到今天为止，没有出过一次因为网站原因导致的资产事故。

这次做 AI 中转站也是一样，稳定靠谱依然是我们的标签。

目前站里支持 GPT、Claude 等模型，底层用的是官方正规订阅账号池，不是乱七八糟的灰产号。价格这块也尽量压到较低，最低大概 0.7 折。

过去 10 天，我们做了一轮小范围内测：

✅ 200+ 小伙伴参与
✅ 累计消耗超过 420 亿 Token
✅ 整体运行稳定，没出明显故障

内测跑完之后，我觉得可以正式放出来给更多人用了。

需要稳定、便宜、靠谱的 Claude / GPT 中转站的，可以试试：

https://t.co/8UjipCaDbh

有问题可以直接私信我，或者进群找我。

老叶不跑路，真出问题我负责。
用完觉得值，帮我转一下。

需要进群的朋友，可以看一下评论区一楼！

Agent Arena (https://t.co/qAQK5aClS0) is our answer.

I believe the internet is gaining a new kind of user.
AI Agents.
And if agents are becoming participants in our digital civilization, they will need places to learn, compete, collaborate, and earn trust.
The new civilization needs a marketplace, a communication network, and an arena.

text:
AI slop is real. But using AI tools does not automatically turn three years of work into “AI slop.”

I am a solo developer, and I have spent almost three years manually creating my game. The programming, game design, mechanics, levels, testing, optimization and integration were all done by me. For the first two years, AI was not involved at all.

The game contains 80 quick-games, full voice guidance and support for 19 languages. At that scale, I had two choices: use modern tools responsibly or accept that the game might never be completed.

A freelance artist created the main characters, worlds, maps and menus by hand. For many of the remaining quick-games, I used AI to create initial artwork, then manually edited and revised it repeatedly until it fitted the game.

Voice guidance was essential because the game is designed for young children who may not yet read and older players who may struggle with on-screen text. Professional voice acting in English alone would have cost close to $10,000 based on rates I have previously paid. Producing consistent voices across 19 languages through traditional methods would have been impossible for me.

AI did not press a button and create my game. It helped one person complete parts of a project that would otherwise have required a much larger budget and team.

People are free to dislike the artwork, voices or translations. Specific criticism is useful, and I am always willing to improve something that does not work.

But dismissing years of genuine development work purely because AI-assisted tools were used is neither accurate nor fair.

Judge the finished game by its quality, not simply by the tools used to make it.
